solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Those waking up after trouble initially flares?

indicators.note: after sends the waking-up word second, behind the initial letter
initially means only the opening letter of the word trouble is taken

parts.note: rousers are people who wake others, or who rouse themselves

explanation.surface: People woken by some disturbance flare up in anger at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flares' looks like a verb about tempers; it is the noun for wide-bottomed legwear, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Flares are a style of legwear widening below the knee, an example of the general garment.

clue.text: Spanish city festival recalled up in Massachusetts

indicators.note: in places the turned festival word within the state's two-letter abbreviation

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Massachusetts

indicators.note: recalled and up, in a down clue, both say the festival word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration or event

explanation.surface: A Spanish city's fiesta is fondly remembered by people in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: Málaga is a port city on Spain's Costa del Sol, birthplace of Picasso.

clue.text: Sweet pea still out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of pea still are put out of order

explanation.surface: A sweet pea, the garden flower, is still not in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet pea' reads as the flower, but 'Sweet' is the definition and 'pea still' the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small chewy or medicated lozenge, a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Auditor's full agreement

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this is the word as heard, not as written

parts.note: packed means crammed full

explanation.surface: An accountant's comprehensive agreement, as if signing off a set of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant; here it means a listener, signalling a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal treaty or deal between parties, a synonym of agreement.

clue.text: Care is on revised plan

indicators.note: revised signals the letters of Care is on are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Care has been taken over a plan that has now been updated.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline or projected sequence of events, effectively a plan.

clue.text: One behind bars in pub mentioned pal

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the pub word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a mate is a pal, a friend

explanation.surface: A prisoner, chatting in the pub, mentions a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pub bars, but it means prison bars.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a prisoner, someone locked in a cell behind bars.

clue.text: Vegetable vessel overturned

indicators.note: overturned, in a down clue, says the vessel word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a keel is a flat-bottomed barge, as used on the River Tyne

explanation.surface: A vegetable container has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a bowl; here it is a boat, the keel or coal barge.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is an allium vegetable related to the onion, a national emblem of Wales.

clue.text: Some characters in Gibraltar mad about Spanish ships

indicators.note: Some characters in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: People in Gibraltar are crazy about the ships of Spain, with a nod to Gibraltar's contested history.
explanation.definitionFit: The Armada was the fleet of warships Spain sent against England in 1588.

clue.text: Afternoon refreshment for the elite?

parts.note: the elite are the cream of society, so their afternoon refreshment is jokingly their tea

explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is an afternoon meal of scones with jam and clotted cream, served with a pot of tea; the cream is also the elite.

clue.text: Fish and a loaf brought back

indicators.note: brought back says the letters of a plus the head word are reversed

parts.note: loaf is slang for the head, as is nut

explanation.surface: Fish and a loaf of bread are fetched home, perhaps for sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like bread; it is slang for the head (as in 'use your loaf'), which is also NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish, widely eaten, an example of fish.

clue.text: Fitting a small part

parts.note: PT is the abbreviation of part, small signalling a shortened form

explanation.surface: An actor is fitted for a minor role in a production.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means appropriate or suitable, a synonym of the adjective fitting.

clue.text: Mother upset about father backing image

indicators.note: about says the rearranged mother letters go round the reversed father word
upset says the letters of Mother are disturbed into a new order
backing says the father word is read backwards

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A mother is upset that a father supports a particular image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but signals a reversal; 'upset' makes the anagram METHOR, which goes 'about' the turned father.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor is a figure of speech, a verbal picture or figurative image.

clue.text: Row after boss gets a title

indicators.note: after places the row word behind the boss word

parts.note: the head is the boss, the person in charge
a line is a row of things

explanation.surface: After a quarrel, the boss is awarded an honorific title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line, as in a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the heading printed above a newspaper story, its title.

clue.text: Rebecca's son seen in smoke sauna

indicators.note: seen in says the answer can be found inside the letters of smoke sauna

explanation.surface: A man is spotted in a steamy, smoky sauna.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Rebecca bore twin sons, Jacob and his elder brother, the hairy hunter.

clue.text: Diplomatic specialist, democrat, is spoken for

parts.note: an attaché is an embassy official with a specialist area, such as a military attaché
D is the abbreviation for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: An embassy expert, a Democrat, is already taken by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spoken for is in a relationship, i.e. committed to a partner, not single.

clue.text: Distinctive theories one added to text message

indicators.note: added to puts the numeral piece in front of the message abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
SMS is the standard short message service, a text message

explanation.surface: Someone adds a distinctive theory to a text they are sending.
explanation.definitionFit: Isms are doctrines or ideologies, named by suffix as in Marxism or feminism.

clue.text: Mal is a silly sausage!

indicators.note: silly means the letters of Mal is a are muddled around

explanation.surface: Mal is being a silly sausage, a fond rebuke for a daft person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly sausage' is a British jokey term for a foolish person; here 'sausage' is the definition and 'silly' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, spiced Italian sausage, an example of the meat product.

clue.text: A job worried religious dissident

parts.note: a post is a job or position
ate means worried or troubled, as in 'what's eating you'

explanation.surface: A job left a religious dissenter anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is past-tense ATE in the sense of eating at someone, nagging them.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who renounces their religious faith, a dissenter from it.

clue.text: Refuse to eat hard batter

indicators.note: to eat says the rubbish word takes the hard letter inside it

parts.note: trash is refuse, rubbish
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to eat a stiff pancake batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish; 'batter' looks like a cooking mixture but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash is to beat or strike repeatedly, a synonym of the verb batter.

clue.text: It's a plus but often comes between partners

definitions.meaning: the plus sign, as in two plus two, means the joining word
in names of firms or couples the joining word stands between the two names, as in Marks & Spencer

explanation.surface: Something is a benefit yet often drives a wedge between partners.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction is spoken for the plus sign and links paired names, like Laurel & Hardy.

clue.text: Pop to see Oscar's successor

definitions.meaning: pop is an informal word for father
in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for P follows Oscar, the code word for O

explanation.surface: Dad goes to meet the person taking over from Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa is a childish word for father and the radio code word for the letter P.

clue.text: Allowed to drink fine port

indicators.note: to drink says the allowed word takes the fine letter inside it

parts.note: let means allowed, permitted
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to drink a good glass of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the fortified wine but is the nautical word for the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, port is the left-hand side when facing forward, the opposite of starboard.

clue.text: One gets right in front — to win it?

definitions.text: One gets right in front — to win it?

indicators.note: in front puts the right letter before the one word

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: A competitor surges right to the front, perhaps to win a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word; R goes in front of ACE. The whole clue also describes what a contest is about.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a contest of speed in which competitors try to get ahead and win.

clue.text: Short piece of writing with plot gets a tick?

parts.note: a para, short for paragraph, is a short piece of writing
a site is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A short essay with a good storyline earns a teacher's approving mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick' looks like a teacher's mark of approval; it is the blood-sucking creature, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a bloodsucking arachnid living on a host animal, an example of such an organism.

clue.text: Fan outside set, somehow, for tie

indicators.note: outside says the letters of fan go around the reworked set
somehow says the letters of set are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: A fan outside the film set is somehow wearing a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like an admirer but is taken as letters; 'somehow' gives STE, which sits between its second and third letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten is to secure or bind something, synonymous with the verb tie.

clue.text: Make clear list of passengers

definitions.meaning: to make clear is to show or reveal plainly
a ship's or aircraft's document listing its passengers and cargo

explanation.surface: Clarify the list of who is travelling on board.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means display or reveal; as a noun it is a vessel's cargo and passenger list.
